goal: Is ke baad aap do ya zyada conditions ko &&, || aur ! se jod sakenge, truth table se result predict kar sakenge, sahi range check likh sakenge, aur short-circuit evaluation samjha sakenge.
warmup: Exam roll number slip lene ke liye office kehta hai: 'Aap ke paas fee challan AUR student card dono hone chahiye.' Agar sirf ek ho, to slip nahi milti. Ground mein free entry ke liye rule yeh ho sakta hai: 'Students YA staff.' Koi bhi ek kaafi hai. Aur ek dukaan ka board kehta hai 'Sunday ko open NAHI.' Real life mein AND, OR aur NOT pehle se use hote hain. C++ bhi yehi ideas use karta hai taake ek hi if mein ek se zyada cheezein check ho sakein.
definition: Compound condition do ya zyada simple conditions ko jodti hai. C++ mein teen logical operators hain. && ka matlab AND hai: sirf tab true jab dono taraf true hon. || ka matlab OR hai: true jab kam az kam ek taraf true ho. ! ka matlab NOT hai: yeh condition ko ulat deta hai, yaani true false ho jata hai aur false true ho jata hai. Har logical operator ka result bool hota hai, yaani true ya false.
howItWorks: Computer compound condition ko left se right parhta hai aur precedence order use karta hai: pehle !, phir arithmetic, phir relational (< <= > >=), phir equality (== !=), phir &&, aur aakhir mein ||. Is liye a || b && c ka matlab a || (b && c) hai. Jab bhi shak ho, brackets lagayein. C++ short-circuit evaluation bhi use karta hai: jaise hi jawab pata chal jaye, woh ruk jata hai. A && B mein, agar A false ho, to B kabhi check nahi hota. A || B mein, agar A true ho, to B kabhi check nahi hota. Doosri example ka trace chalayein aur dekhein ke is wajah se ek function run NAHI hota.
